title: Adaptive output fragmentation and local tool proxies PRD (wip)
content:
Overview:
This doc proposes an incremental PRD for two tightly-coupled features: (1) adaptive output fragmentation for streaming responses so clients can consume prioritized partial results with a clear commit model; and (2) a lightweight, ephemeral local tool-proxy concept that reduces round-trip latency for tool-like actions (web lookups, small DB reads, user-tokenized calls) while preserving hosted control plane guarantees. The goal is improved perceived latency for interactive flows, better client-side ergonomics for partial/structured output, and clearer failure/fallback semantics for tool calling.

Context / motivation:
- Many host-side streaming flows are dominated by the last-mile latency when the response requires external tool calls (e.g., search, calculator, or customer-specific DB lookup).
- Clients today either (a) wait for a final JSON/structured payload, or (b) stitch a series of plain-text partial updates without a reliable notion of which fragments are authoritative. Both hurt UX and make SDKs brittle.
- We can improve interactive UX by returning prioritized fragments (e.g., title -> top-3 bullets -> detailed evidence) and letting clients render progressively. While tool invocations can still be centralized, placing a short-lived, RBAC-limited proxy near the client allows many simple tool operations to complete in <20–50ms instead of hundreds.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Median time to first meaningful fragment in interactive LLM sessions reduced by 25% for targeted customers.
- 50% of customer sessions that include small tool calls use the local proxy fallback in regions where proxy is enabled (experiment %).
- SDK error surface simplified: fewer than 15% of instrumented apps need custom retry logic for partial fragments after launch.

Non-goals:
- This does not replace Dedicated/private-hosted tool integrations that require strict data residency.
- We are not building a full general-purpose edge compute runtime (no arbitrary code execution). Proxies are limited to connector patterns we approve.

Constraints and guardrails:
- Security: proxies must never hold long-term secrets. Use short-lived delegation tokens with explicit scopes.
- Observability: every fragment and tool call must include trace ids + token count estimates to allow cost/latency attribution in Console.
- Consistency: final committed fragment must be recoverable from server-side logs; proxies may provide optimistic results but the platform must validate/commit or roll them back when necessary.

User stories:
1) Product manager (web): a user types a long prompt; app shows title immediately, then top bullets, then inline evidence. If a tool lookup fails, the UI shows best-effort text and a "retry with hosted" CTA.
2) Mobile developer: wants a small SDK surface that receives fragment callbacks and deals with network toggles gracefully. Should be able to render offline-progressive snapshots.
3) Platform operator: needs per-customer telemetry showing which fragments were proxy-sourced vs hosted-sourced and cost delta.

Design: adaptive output fragmentation
- Fragment model: a response is an ordered sequence of frames. Each frame has: id, type (summary|item|evidence|commit), priority (0..100), partial=true|false, and optional schema hint (json-schema id).
- Commit semantics: commit frame indicates server-acknowledged stable state for a subset of the response. Clients should treat earlier frames as speculative until commit arrives for that scope.
- Progressive typing: producers can tag fragments as incremental-updates or replacements. Replacement fragments include a replace_of field (id of earlier fragment) to allow reconciliation.
- Example streaming sequence (pseudo):
  - F1: {id=f1, type=summary, partial=true, priority=90, text='Plan: 3 steps...'}
  - F2: {id=f2, type=item, partial=true, priority=70, text='Step 1: call search'}
  - Tool invocation dispatched (proxy or hosted)
  - F3: {id=f3, type=evidence, partial=true, priority=50, text='Search result preview...'}
  - F4: {id=f4, type=commit, partial=false, priority=100, scope=[f1,f2,f3]}
- Backpressure and flow-control: server sends a header with estimated token budget per fragment stream. SDKs expose a high-water/low-water mark and allow application code to subscribe to "first-meaningful-fragment" events.

Design: local tool-proxy model
- Purpose: handle latency-sensitive, low-data-volume tool calls (search index query with small payload, ephemeral session DB reads, user-context enrichers).
- Deployment: regional ephemeral proxies (managed as a lightweight container pool) or edge lambda-style ephemeral hosts in cloud regions. Not shipped to customer VPC by default.
- Security model:
  - Delegation token flow: hosted API issues a scoped token (15s–2m TTL) to the client SDK that binds a session id, allowed connector ids, and max qps.
  - All proxy requests are logged and signed; server validates any proxy-originated result before committing into the canonical response.
- Failure/fallback: if proxy returns an error or doesn't respond before a per-invocation timeout, the platform transparently re-issues the tool call from the hosted backend (with same intent) and marks resulting fragments as hosted_sourced.
- Idempotency and dedup: proxy calls include client-generated idempotency key; hosted call must be able to detect and deduplicate if both fire.

API and SDK ergonomics (client-facing):
- High-level call: generateStream(prompt, options) returns a StreamHandle. The StreamHandle exposes:
  - onFragment(fn(fragment)) called for every fragment
  - onCommit(fn(commit)) called when server commit frame arrives
  - firstMeaningful() promise resolves on first fragment above thresholds
  - resumeFrom(commit_id) to resume replay after reconnect
  - suggestProxyPolicy(): SDK can request scoped proxy token from the control plane when running in eligible regions
- Example pseudocode (JS):
  const stream = client.generateStream({prompt});
  stream.onFragment(f => renderDelta(f));
  stream.onCommit(c => markStable(c.scope));
  await stream.firstMeaningful(); // show preview
- Backwards compatibility: default mode remains current streaming protocol; clients opt into fragments & proxy via a header (X-RW-Fragment=1). Beta SDKs will enable heuristics to opt in for interactive templates.

Server-side validation and reconciliation:
- Any proxy-sourced fragment is flagged with metadata (proxy_id, token). The server verifies signature and accepts optimistic fragment for immediate streaming, but still executes a canonical hosted validation:
  - If hosted validation result differs materially, the server emits a replacement fragment and a delta commit explaining the change.
  - All commits include a signed digest of the canonical payload for audit.

Observability and billing:
- Telemetry fields to emit per-fragment: fragment_id, source(proxy|hosted), tokens_est, tokens_billed, latency_ms, trace_id, customer_id, model_id.
- Console: add a per-route "fragment distribution" chart (time to first fragment, time to commit, % proxy-sourced).
- Billing: proxy-sourced fragments still billed to customer; show a discounted estimated infra-surcharge in dedicated views (experimental).

SLOs and safety:
- Proxy TTL for delegation tokens: default 60s, min 15s, configurable by security team.
- Consistency SLO: <2% of committed fragments should require replacement within 1 minute due to proxy-to-host reconciliation (initial target).
- Safety checks: proxies cannot call connectors marked as `sensitive` (PCI/PHI) unless explicit enterprise enablement and private deployment.

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha: platform + SDK changes behind feature flag; experiments with 3 product integrations (search, FAQ-index, simple calculator).
2) Beta customers: invite 10 customers (GTM and PM selection) with opt-in control via Console per project.
3) Public: enable as opt-in header; allow SDKs to auto-opt heuristics for interactive templates.

Developer experience notes / checklist:
- SDK must expose simple fragment abstraction and safe default behavior: do not auto-apply speculative fragments to persisted state without an explicit commit.
- Provide a React/Android/iOS component set for progressive rendering (Title, List, Evidence) to lower integration friction.
- Add migration docs: how to move from plain stream.on('data') to fragment model.

Open questions / risks:
- How to surface legal/audit trail for proxy-sourced results for regulated customers? (Need KMS pattern + audit retention change).
- Are latency wins worth the added complexity in the SDK surface? We should prototype end-to-end and track "integration time" metric.
- Cost model for proxies: who pays infra? Initially Redwood bears infra cost for experiments; explore surcharge model later.
- Edge regions: which cloud providers / regions do we support for alpha? (to discuss with infra).

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Engineering (Marco Li): spike: implement proxy token flow + signed optimistic fragment (2 weeks).
- SDK (Evan Wu): prototype JS SDK API + React progressive components (2 weeks).
- Product (Priya): prepare beta customer list and Console toggle UI spec (1 week).
- Security (Sofia): threat model and token TTL recommendation (1 week).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a short runbook for proxy outage behavior for customer support.
- Add sample low-level wireframes for fragment JSON schema in Confluence.
- Coordinate with billing to start tracking proxy infra costs separately.

References / related docs:
- hosted-api/streaming-handshake-v2 (confluence)
- SDK progressive rendering components (internal playground)
- Product notes: “low-touch-tool-routing-and-structured-streaming-prd" (see linked artifacts)

End.
